subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — follow-up and perf/throughput clarification
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@finpay.com>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@finpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — follow-up and perf/throughput clarification

Hi Liam — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + a recommended path: 

Summary of FinPay requirements (from today's call):
- Primary workload: real-time fraud scoring + conversational support (short completions + reranking).
- Sustained average: ~200 requests/sec (avg request = ~120 input tokens, expected output ~350 tokens).
- Peak spikes: up to ~350 requests/sec (bursty around payroll cutoffs).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250 ms for the short-path scoring calls; p95 < 400 ms acceptable for longer conversational responses.
- Security: corporate SRE asked about VPC/private options for production.

Quick recommendation:
- PoC / evaluation: start on Hosted API to validate quality and integration (fastest onboarding).
- Production for low-latency, predictable cost and throughput: we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) given sustained 200+ QPS and bursty spikes — Dedicated gives predictable throughput, pre-warmed KV caches, and lower tail latency.
- Private/VPC: available as a follow-up for enterprise deployment (Private is typically used for strict network isolation / on-prem).

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical perf test: Redwood SE can run a 48-hour perf test using a sample traffic profile you provide (we'll use a dedicated test pool with the same model/quantization settings).
2) Pricing & SOW: attached initial proposal and SOW draft for Dedicated capacity (ballpark numbers included).
3) Technical deep-dive: schedule a 60min session with our infra SEs to walk through autoscaling, warmup behavior, and integration details.

Questions I had after the call (helpful if you can confirm):
- Are the 200 QPS sustained across the day or concentrated in 2-3 hourly peaks?
- Do you expect payload sizes to change significantly (e.g., longer contexts) in the near term?

I've attached the proposal + draft SOW. Happy to adjust based on answers — can schedule the perf test as early as next week.

Best,

Thanks Neha — appreciate the summary. A few quick clarifications from SRE + product: 

- The 200 QPS figure is sustained during business hours (09:00-18:00 ET) with two predictable spikes (end of day payroll windows) that last ~15–30 minutes and can hit ~350 QPS.
- Payload sizes are stable for the scoring calls; long-form convo usage is a smaller percentage (~15% of traffic).
- Security: our SRE asked if Dedicated buys any more control over networking/warm caches vs Hosted, or if we should be looking at Private/VPC immediately.
- Also need a rough cost band for Dedicated (monthly committed tier vs pay-as-you-go hosted).

If you can provide answers to the above and a short summary cost band that would help with our internal procurement conversation. Happy to have Marissa join the deep-dive.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — follow-up and perf/throughput clarification

Liam — thanks for the answers, helpful context. Answers inline and next steps below.

- Networking / control: Dedicated gives more predictable, reserved GPU capacity and comes with isolated pools (no noisy neighbors). It also provides pre-warmed KV/cache behavior because you can keep workers pinned to your model instances; that materially reduces cold-start and tail latency vs a purely multi-tenant Hosted pool for sustained workloads. Private/VPC is a separate offering if you need customer-managed networking or on-prem — typically elected for compliance, not performance alone.

- Warmup/spikes: Dedicated + reserved headroom is the safest for sustained 200 QPS + 350 QPS spikes. We also support autoscaling for burst capacity, but autoscale has some scale-up latency; reserved capacity ensures the capacity is already there for immediate spikes. For the perf test we propose a stepped load profile that reproduces your payroll spike to validate tail behavior.

- Cost band (high-level):
  - Hosted (pay-as-you-go): lower upfront, higher per-token execution cost — good for PoC/early integration.
  - Dedicated (committed): higher fixed monthly commit but substantially lower per-token/unit cost at scale and predictable billing. For a sustained 200 QPS workload with your token sizes (avg 470 tokens/response incl. input), rough estimate: $60k–$95k/month committed (depends on model family and quantization profile). This is a ballpark; proposal table attached has example tiers.

Next steps:
1) Schedule perf test: Marissa/Dylan + your SRE — please share two 1-hour windows this week.
2) I'll circulate an updated SOW with two committed-tier options (conservative headroom vs optimized) and a check-box for VPC evaluation.
3) If procurement wants a 2-week Dedicated evaluation, we can include a short-term promo in the SOW for an evaluation period.

If that looks good I'll lock in a time for the perf test and have our SEs prep the test harness.
